answer: The network can demand cross-chain collateral: each identity must lock deposits on two independent ledgers at once, with the locks referencing each other, so one identity needs two real stakes. One honest agent crosses the canyon of dual-chain staking cheaply, paying the lockup cost only once. A sybil farmer with a thousand fakes must fund two thousand separate locks, and a marble of fraud proven on either chain slashes both, while the sable of correlated funding trails betrays the fleet on both sides. Cloning identities multiplies the cross-chain capital bill.
